questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping will be easier.
Stopping will take longer.
You cannot stop.
Stopping is about the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping will take longer.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle. Extra weight requires more braking power to stop. Going downhill also makes stopping slower. Combined, these factors make stopping take much longer.

questions.question: Where is a motorcycle most likely to have a conflict with other vehicles?

options.text: Intersections
Highways
Parking lots
Residential areas

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersections
questions.explanation: Intersections are the most dangerous places for motorcycles. Other vehicles often cross into your path at intersections. Stay alert and watch for vehicles that may cross in front of you.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking on a good road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
Release the rear brake and use only the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you stop completely.
questions.explanation: Keep the rear brake locked until you stop. Your motorcycle will stay under control as long as it stays upright and travels in a straight line.

questions.question: If a driver is following you too closely, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry about them.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.
Speed up.
Get off the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. If you speed up, the driver may just tailgate you at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When making a turn, how much traction is available for stopping?

options.text: Less traction is available.
More traction is available.
The same amount as on a straight road.
You should never try to stop while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less traction is available.
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle leans to turn, some traction is used for turning. This means less traction is left for braking. Brake while turning only with great care.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what formation keeps riders close while maintaining safe space?

options.text: Pairs
Staggered formation
Single-file line
Passing formation

questions.correctAnswerText: Staggered formation
questions.explanation: A staggered formation allows riders to stay together while keeping safe space around each rider. Use a single-file line only when turning, in curves, or on highways. Never ride side-by-side.

questions.question: How can a motorcycle rider prevent other drivers from sharing the lane?

options.text: Give dirty looks to other drivers.
Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left side of the lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves no large spaces on either side. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share your lane.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what must you do?

options.text: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
You can finish a pass in a no-passing zone if you started before the zone began.
You can exceed the speed limit.
Pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Complete the pass without exceeding the speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must follow the posted speed limit. You can only pass where passing is allowed.

questions.question: Why should loads be placed low on a motorcycle?

options.text: A high load raises the center of gravity.
A high load may block the turn signals.
You may not be able to see over a high load.
Others cannot see a low load.

questions.correctAnswerText: A high load raises the center of gravity.
questions.explanation: A load placed too high raises your motorcycle's center of gravity. This affects balance and control.

questions.question: What is one way to reduce your risk of crashing?

options.text: Use your turn signals to show you plan to change lanes.
Tailgate other drivers.
Look only 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Do not use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals to show you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use turn signals to tell other drivers your plans. Be visible, maintain safe space, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready for changing conditions. These steps reduce crash risk.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right with no oncoming traffic on your left, you should:

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more often than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. If traffic is coming toward you, stay in the center of your lane.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.
Ride under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: To stop quickly, you should:

options.text: Reduce throttle and use the front brake.
Use the rear brake only.
Use the front brake only.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used when you need to stop quickly.
Should only be used on slippery surfaces.
Is not as effective as the rear brake.
Is safe to use when used properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is safe to use when used properly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes any time you slow or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when you use it properly.

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Only take a few minutes.
Take more than an hour.
Be complicated to perform.
Not be done before every ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only take a few minutes.
questions.explanation: Do a thorough inspection of your motorcycle before every ride. It usually takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Reduce your speed.
Increase your following distance.
Decrease your following distance.
Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your following distance.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam, except when you are following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: To lean a motorcycle when turning, you should:

options.text: Always press on the left handgrip.
Always press on the right handgrip.
Press on the handgrip opposite the direction of the turn.
Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press on the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To make the motorcycle lean, press on the handgrip in the direction you want to turn.

questions.question: When entering a curve, a group should ride in:

options.text: A single-file formation.
A staggered formation.
Pairs.
On the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: While staggered formation is usually best, switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: Which of the following is not safe for preventing fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain
Taking artificial stimulants
Limiting how much you ride in one day
Taking frequent breaks

questions.correctAnswerText: Taking artificial stimulants
questions.explanation: On long trips, take frequent breaks to rest and limit riding to six hours per day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain because they increase tiredness. Do not take artificial stimulants because the crash after they wear off is very dangerous.

questions.question: More than half of all crashes:

options.text: Happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
Happen at night.
Are caused by worn tires.
Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve riders with less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders who have had their motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the wobble.
Use the brakes slowly.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
Shift to a lower gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up during a wobble—this makes it worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly release the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: Is it legal to ride between two vehicles that are moving in the same direction?

options.text: No, it is illegal.
Yes, if traffic is heavy.
Yes, during the day to help traffic flow.
Yes, if the rider feels comfortable doing it.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, it is illegal.
questions.explanation: In Oregon, motorcycles and mopeds cannot pass between two moving vehicles on a multilane highway or one-way street. This practice is illegal.

questions.question: At what point does alcohol impair your ability to ride safely?

options.text: Before you reach the legal limit.
Once you reach the legal limit.
Just above the legal limit.
Well above the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you reach the legal limit.
questions.explanation: Any amount of alcohol can impair your riding ability. Skills needed to ride safely are affected well before you reach the legal limit. Never ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: Riders without helmets are ________ to die in a crash than riders with helmets.

options.text: Half as likely
Twice as likely
Three times as likely
Just as likely

questions.correctAnswerText: Three times as likely
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets. This is true no matter the speed.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen better.
Help you avoid hazards on the road.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you safe by staying out of blind spots, helping you see and be seen, avoiding road hazards, avoiding wind from other vehicles, and giving you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from trying to share your lane with you.
